correctness.rationale: A line-contained basis factors through scalar projection. Completeness forces essential injectivity; the projected absolutely continuous spectral measure has constant density. Rescaling its line direction therefore gives \(|\langle u,v_j\rangle|=c_j\) and Lebesgue measure on two disjoint intervals of total length one. Łaba's exhaustive two-interval theorem then gives exactly the integer-gap lattice branch and the equal-mass two-coset branch. The converse follows from the projection theorem. The concrete exceptional skew example is replayed by the packaged verifier.

value.rationale: The recent weighted paper proves existence but leaves the family of line spectra in the intrinsically three-dimensional non-coplanar case unspecified. A complete classification is a natural structural question. The result gives a sharp dichotomy: unequal segment masses force every line spectrum to be a lattice, while equal masses are exactly the regime permitting a two-coset non-lattice branch. It also produces an explicit non-lattice line spectrum for the source's basic skew example.
